recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Reverting to FHIR-7898's original 0..1 or example-binding details would contradict later published OO decisions; future category changes should be handled by a new tracker or an explicit reconciliation of the later category issues.
issue_request: FHIR-7898 was a Published OO change request from the DSTU1 era asking for clearer support for querying subsets of Observations such as vitals, labs, imaging, and social history. The approved resolution was to add Observation.category as a searchable CodeableConcept, originally 0..1.
initial_application: The request was applied in 2015 by dba136eacbbb, which added Observation.category and the category token search parameter; 4e55d97ce3b0 refined the category text and examples; and 158840613957 added valueset-observation-category.xml.
additional_context: Observation is active in source/fhir.ini, so the Observation StructureDefinition and search-parameter bundle are current build inputs. The current source uses max=* and preferred binding because FHIR-9543 later approved changing category from 0..1 to 0..*, and FHIR-9857 later approved changing the binding from example to preferred. FHIR-10006 documents the category intent as broad standard buckets that support searching even when clients do not understand Observation.code, with multiple orthogonal grouping axes allowed.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build already provides Observation.category as a 0..* CodeableConcept with a preferred binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/observation-category, and the category token SearchParameter targets Observation.category.

related_jiras.note: Changed Observation.category from 0..1 to 0..* and explains why the current cardinality supersedes the original FHIR-7898 wording.
Changed the Observation.category binding from example to preferred, explaining the current binding strength.
Answered category-intent questions by confirming broad search buckets and multiple orthogonal grouping axes.
Later lastN/last-known discussions use category as a filter but concern a separate operation/search feature.
